title: Walking the Schrödinger Bridge: A Direct Trajectory for Text-to-3D Generation
motivation: SDS requires high CFG values causing over-saturation/over-smoothing artifacts, while low-CFG variants fail on 3DGS
problem_framing: Learning optimal direct transport trajectory between current rendering distribution and target distribution
key_insight: SDS is a special case of Schrödinger Bridge—when endpoint is Gaussian noise, Schrödinger Bridge score collapses to SDS score function
method_signature: TraCe constructs diffusion bridge from current rendering to text-conditioned denoised target, trains LoRA on bridge score dynamics
evaluation_criteria: CLIP Score, GPTEval3D, ImageReward, visual quality comparison with CFG=20
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Very low CFG (e.g., 5) yields reduced visual fidelity; results stable only at CFG ~15-20
evidence_for_taste: score estimates are noisy and not guaranteed to represent optimal direction for 3D optimization
forces the optimization process to cope with score functions optimized for 2D image generation
requires large-scale, high-quality 3D datasets required for direct supervised training
not strictly correspond to the gradient of a well-defined probability distribution
naive Schrödinger Bridge approach results in comparatively smoother, less detailed rendering
thinking_moves: Theoretical derivation connecting SDS to Schrödinger Bridge via score function equivalence
Reformulating optimization as explicit bridge construction between rendering endpoints
Bridging gap between noisy 2D score estimates and optimal transport path learning
Decomposing optimization into explicit trajectory sampling and LoRA-based score learning
